instrument: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02 R4 (GNSS outage and alterations)
edition_or_version: Revision 4, 3 July 2026 (replaces R3 of 5 July 2024; first issued 17 Mar 2022)
status_note: Informational bulletin; recommendations not mandatory; further safety/airworthiness directive may follow
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends recurrent training of flight crews and relevant ops personnel; assessing risks of losing onboard GNSS; before flights into known affected areas, ensuring GNSS-backup systems are not MEL-inoperative and MEL backups do not rely on GNSS; planning non-GNSS procedures where practical; verifying position by non-GNSS means and navaid availability (jamming); monitoring non-GNSS navaids/EPU and GNSS vs non-GNSS time (spoofing); using flight data monitoring where required.
Asks operators to file AIREPs for GNSS anomalies, report safety-impacting events under Reg (EU) 376/2014 and report suspected spoofing and higher-risk jamming to manufacturers.

requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems must be designed so humans can effectively oversee them; oversight scaled to risk, autonomy and context; overseers must be able to understand limits, notice anomalies and automation bias, override or reverse outputs, and stop the system safely.
